answer: Peers re-execute a random sample of work without being told which sample. Three unrelated confirmations are required before a score lands. Quorum must span at least two subnetworks, so a single host cannot grade its own output. Re-execution costs the auditor one run per sample, and the attacker pays for every seat that fails. A 1,000-seat farm faces a re-run on each identity, three signatures each, and a quorum it cannot fill from one provider. The sable of a hidden farm shows on the second subnetwork, the pulse of a fake score stops at the third check, and the violet of duplicate work fades.
